#### **Key Takeaways**


- Technology is helping foodservice operators meet rising guest expectations without compromising service.


- AI and connected guest data make it easier to recognize preferences and personalize interactions at scale.


- The most effective foodservice technology works behind the scenes, empowering staff while staying invisible to guests.


Great foodservice has never been just about the food.


Whether it’s a quick-service restaurant, a university dining hall, a hotel outlet, or a healthcare facility, operators have always focused on balancing quality, efficiency, and personal service. However, guest expectations continue to evolve. Consumers have grown accustomed to experiences that are increasingly personalized, convenient, and responsive to their preferences. As a result, they increasingly bring those same expectations into foodservice environments.


The fundamentals haven’t changed. Operators are still focused on delivering great food and service, while guests continue to value convenience, quality, and personal attention. As expectations evolve, operators are looking for new ways to deliver those experiences while making interactions faster and more personalized.


#### **Removing Friction from the Experience**


Whether it’s a student moving between classes, an employee grabbing lunch between meetings, a patient ordering a meal in a healthcare facility, or a guest in a busy hospitality venue, the common expectation is the same: people want foodservice to fit into their schedule, not the other way around.


Mobile ordering has been one of the biggest steps toward meeting that expectation. Rather than waiting in line or searching for an available cashier, guests can browse menus, customize orders, pay, and pick up their meals using their own device. But mobile ordering is only part of a larger evolution.


Operators are exploring new ways to make interactions even more intuitive. Instead of navigating screens and menus, guests may increasingly interact through conversation. Rather than scrolling through categories or searching for specific items, they simply state what they want:


“Order my usual salad.”


“Can I get a turkey sandwich with no tomatoes?”


“What’s a good high-protein option for lunch today?”


With this highly conversational – and more convenient – approach, the underlying technology fades into the background and the interaction becomes more natural.


#### **The Next Opportunity Is Understanding the Guest**


Convenience may drive adoption, but personalization is what makes an experience feel memorable.


Most digital ordering experiences still present every guest with essentially the same app journey: the same menu, the same recommendations, the same promotions. Yet anyone who has worked in foodservice understands that guests are not all the same. Some order the same meal every visit. Some have dietary restrictions. Some prefer specific ingredients or preparation styles. Some order breakfast five days a week and never visit during dinner hours.


Historically, recognizing these patterns depended on employee memory and local knowledge. As guest data becomes more connected, AI can help surface those insights more consistently across thousands of guest interactions. In this way, technology gives foodservice organizations the details they need to create experiences that feel more relevant to the individual.


Returning guests can reorder favorites in seconds, receive more relevant promotions, and discover recommendations that align with their preferences. Instead of spending time searching through menus, they can move more quickly from decision to experience. Beyond simply streamlining transactions, technology can help foodservice operators remember guests at a scale that would otherwise be impossible.


#### **Better Information Creates Better Service**


One of the most practical applications of AI may have less to do with guests and more to do with employees. Foodservice teams make hundreds or thousands of service decisions every day, yet employees often have limited visibility into the guest beyond the transaction directly in front of them. Connected guest data and intelligent recommendations help provide additional context.


A returning guest’s preferences become easier to recognize. Dietary considerations become easier to accommodate. Employees gain information that helps them provide more relevant guidance and recommendations. While the interaction remains human, employees are no longer operating without critical guest context.


Service teams already know how to create outstanding guest experiences, but they haven’t always had immediate access to the guest insights that can make service feel more personal and relevant. When guest preferences, order history, and other relevant details are easier to access, employees are better equipped to make every interaction feel informed and personal.


#### **Hospitality Works Best When Technology Gets Out of the Way**


Foodservice has always adopted technology with a simple goal: help people deliver better service. From kitchen display systems and handheld devices to online ordering and mobile payments, the most successful foodservice innovations are the ones that make the experience feel easier while becoming “invisible” to the guest.


The foodservice technologies that have had the greatest impact over the last several decades all share something in common: guests rarely think about them. Few guests notice the systems that route orders through a kitchen, process payments, or synchronize menus across channels. They simply notice when service feels efficient and consistent, or more importantly, if it feels disjointed or unnecessarily slow. AI is unlikely to be any different. Guests won’t care how the technology works behind the scenes. They’ll care whether ordering feels easier, service feels more personal, and interactions feel more seamless than they did before.


When the technology disappears and the hospitality remains, that’s typically a sign the technology is doing its job well.


#### **The Future Is More Personal, Not More Digital**


While much of the recent discussion around AI focuses on the technology itself, foodservice operators are ultimately evaluating it through a much simpler lens: does it help create a better guest experience?


Mobile ordering, intelligent guest profiles, and conversational interfaces all represent new ways to engage with guests, but the underlying objective remains familiar. Operators are still trying to serve guests efficiently, understand individual preferences, and build loyalty over time.


What’s different today is the scale. Guests interact through more channels, expectations continue to rise, and employees are often expected to deliver personalized service across thousands of interactions. AI has the potential to help bridge that gap by making guest insights more accessible and interactions more relevant.


The most interesting aspect of this shift in technology is that it enables foodservice professionals to become better equipped to recognize, remember, and serve guests as individuals. In an industry built on hospitality, that’s a meaningful step forward.


Written By


David Bain


With 10+ years of experience, David specializes in bridging the gap between complex technical integrations and operational success to drive record-breaking business growth.
